newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods - Gasolines mixed, activity quiet.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods - Gasolines mixed, activity quiet.

text.p: Gasoline differentials, both conventional and reformulated, showed little movement in what was quiet activity on Monday, although barrels of RFG remain in tight supply in New York Harbor and the U.S. Gulf Coast.
Meanwhile, NYMEX crude oil weakened in early session on news Iraq submitted its aid distribution plan to the United Nations, bringing the country one step closer to resuming oil sales.
August NYMEX crude oil was down six cents at $19.21 cents a barrel, heating oil was up 0.08 cent at 52.30 cents a gallon and unleaded was off 0.45 cent at 59.60 cents a gallon.
Conventional M2-grade regular gasoline differentials eased in early trade, with nearby barrels talked near 3.00 cents under the August NYMEX futures, down about 0.50 cent traders said.
However, prompt reformulated A2-grade gasoline differentials firmed modestly early Monday, with bids seen at about 1.60 cent over the August NYMEX price.

Reformulated gasoline barrels should remain tight as long as the additive MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether) remained in short supply. Outages at MTBE production facilities as well as strong demand pushed prices sharply up.
Distillate differentials were steady, with ample supplies available to limit any bullish price movement, according to market watchers.

U.S. Gulf gasoline differentials also showed little movement in quiet midday trade. Players said there was little activity ahead of Wednesday's deadline for scheduling shipments along the Colonial Pipeline for M1-grade conventional unleaded.

In thin talk, players pegged M1 at 2.60/2.35 cent below the August NYMEX, about 0.05 cent firmer from Friday. M2-grade, which has a scheduling deadline on Tuesday, was done at 3.75 cent below the Merc.
A1-grade reformulated gasoline also weakened about a quarter cent to 0.75/1.00 cent above August NYMEX. But players said tight supplies on the product may pressure prices up higher this week.
Prompt V1-grade, or 93 premium gasoline, weakened as well.

Midcontinent differentials were quiet and steady in a slow start off to the week. Group Three prompt unleaded gasoline differentials were weaker at 0.50/0.25 cent under NYMEX, continuing last week's more than 1.25 cent loss. Chicago prompt gasoline differentials were unchanged at 0.50/0.25 cent below the print, with 0.30 cent done.
"There is just no activity," said a Chicago player.
